- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 2–3 periods.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model tends to hold too high; adjust downward by 2–4% for next 3–5 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; if sentiment shifts sharply (e.g., from 0.33 to 1.00 or vice versa), adjust forecast 1–3 days ahead to align with sentiment trend.
- If model forecast is consistently 2–4% above true outcome over 3–5 periods, apply a “mean reversion bias” correction — subtract 1–2% from forecast for next 3–5 periods.
